exposure: third-/fourth-degree perineal injuries (obstetric anal sphincter injury, OASI)
Degree of perineal injury (no/first-degree, second-degree, third-/fourth-degree [obstetric anal sphincter injury, OASI]), Cesarean section
outcome: Impact of pelvic floor dysfunction on daily life
cohort: 776 primiparas, of whom 511 (66%) responded to a follow-up questionnaire
finding: Pelvic floor dysfunction was common after childbirth, with increasing severity of perineal injury associated with a higher risk of adverse outcomes, particularly for women with OASI.
mod_finding: Women with third-/fourth-degree perineal injuries (OASI) had significantly higher risks of pelvic floor dysfunction symptoms, including prolapse, urge urinary incontinence, pain, dyspareunia, and impacts on daily life.
